thread:
Marta: CI red on attn-kernel paged+fused matrix build, linking error when producing fused_flash.so :(
Josh: Saw the failure in build-013 too. Any stack/ld output?
Marta: Pasting the tail of the linker log:
```
/usr/bin/ld: fused_flash.o: in function `FlashKernel::run()':
fused_flash.cpp:(.text+0x1a3f): undefined reference to `__cxa_allocate_exception'
/usr/bin/ld: fused_flash.o: undefined reference to `std::bad_alloc::bad_alloc()'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Marta: Build image is our bookworm:gcc-13 base, CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.2
ci-bot: Failed job: attn-paged-fused-linux-x86_64 (node 7) — see logs https://ci.internal/1822/attn-013
Devon: That looks like C++ ABI mismatch or mixing libstdc++ from different toolchains at link time.
Andrew: Did we recently switch the container to debian:bookworm? I remember older images used ubuntu22 + gcc-11.
Sasha: Yup, build matrix changed to gcc-13/bookworm last week to get newer std::span usage.
Kevin: Quick check: run ldd on the produced object libs inside the container — might pick up host libstdc++ via LD_LIBRARY_PATH / explicit rpath.
Josh: Repro steps I used locally (inside container):
```
docker run -it --rm -v $PWD:/src redwood/bookworm-gcc13:cuda12 bash
cd /src/attn
./build.sh --cmake-opts "-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo"
```
Josh: The build fails at link. If I build with -D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0 it moves further but then hits template instantiation errors.
Marta: Not ideal to change ABI. Maybe some prebuilt dependency (protobuf, absl) was built with gcc-11 in cache. Are we pulling wheels from artifacts that embed libstdc++?
Devon: Check the container for /usr/local/lib/libstdc++.so.6. If the binary picks up another version it will show missing GLIBCXX symbols.
Sasha: I ran `strings /usr/local/lib/libstdc++.so.6 | grep GLIBCXX_3.4.29` — it's missing in the container. Host has 3.4.29. So mismatch.
Andrew: Might be our base image uses distro libstdc++ but some wheel we install brought its own bundle.
Marta: Also noticed ccache hit on object files from previous jobs; maybe build cache restored objects produced with older toolchain.
Kevin: Try a clean build (disable cache) and ensure we clear pip wheel cache in CI step before pip install.
Josh: Quick patch: force `-Wl,-rpath,/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13/` in CMake for sanity test — linking succeeds locally but runtime fails with undefined symbol in dynamic loader.
Devon: rpath hack hides underlying problem. We need deterministic toolchain and reproducible deps.
Sasha: Proposal:
- pin base image to redwood/base:bookworm-gcc13-20260201 (immutable digest)
- purge all prebuilt artifacts in CI workspace before build
- add `LD_DEBUG=libs` to failing job to capture where libstdc++ is coming from
- run `readelf -a fused_flash.so | grep NEEDED` to inspect dependencies
Marta: I'll open a quick PR to change the CI job to clean workspace and add LD_DEBUG output.
ci-bot: Marta pushed branch fix/ci-toolchain-clean (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/attn/pulls/188)
Josh: One more oddity: when building the paged variant we enable `-fvisibility=hidden` and `-fno-exceptions` on some translation units. If exception-related symbols are stripped, that could explain `__cxa_allocate_exception` missing.
Andrew: Good point — but that symbol is from libgcc/ABI. If parts compiled with `-fno-exceptions` and others expect exception handling, mixing could cause link errors.
Marta: The linker error shows missing `__cxa_allocate_exception` from fused_flash.o — raising compile flags could help. Which CXX flags do we set for fused target?
Josh: CMake target uses `target_compile_options(fused PRIVATE -O3 -march=native -fno-exceptions)` for perf reasons.
Devon: For now try removing `-fno-exceptions` on fused target in CI to see if linking passes.
Sasha: Also test building fused with `-fPIC`. Some of our compile targets were historically non-PIC and created issues when linking into shared objects.
Kevin: I'm running a matrix job: (clean, no-ccache, remove -fno-exceptions, add -fPIC) — will post results.
ci-bot: Job started: attn-paged-fused-matrix-1822000468
Kevin: Update: removing -fno-exceptions fixed the missing __cxa_allocate_exception but we hit `GLIBCXX_3.4.30` not found at runtime.
Josh: Means we linked against a newer libstdc++ at build time than is available at runtime. Something in the build image or pip deps bundles newer libstdc++.
Marta: Action list for next 24h:
- pin base image digest (Sasha)
- purge cached artifacts and disable ccache for that job (Kevin)
- remove -fno-exceptions and enforce -fPIC for shared libs (Josh)
- add LD_DEBUG and readelf diagnostics (Devon)
- audit pip wheels and prebuilts for bundled libstdc++.so.* (Marta)
Andrew: I can also try building a manylinux wheel variant for the fused kernel and see if that hides native ABI changes.
Sasha: FYI perf numbers: when we got fused working locally with -fno-exceptions we saw ~6% throughput gain on small batches; removing the flag regressed a bit. We'll need to re-tune if we keep exceptions.
Marta: That's acceptable short-term to restore CI. We can recover perf with targeted micro-optimizations later.
Josh: If anyone hits the same errors add `--artifact` logs to the CI ticket. I'll attach my local `ldd`/`readelf` outputs to PR.
Kevin: CI finished: attn-paged-fused-matrix-1822000468 -> partially green. Link errors resolved, runtime GLIBCXX mismatch still on node 3; investigating container image layering.
Devon: Node 3 uses cached docker overlay from older image — sounds like docker daemon on that runner needs image prune.
Marta: I've added a step to force docker pull by digest and `docker system prune -af` on the flaky runners. Will monitor next run.
Sasha: Thanks team. Once CI is stable I can re-run the fused vs paged benchmarks and post perf diffs in #eng-runtime-benchmarks.
Marta: Great. Filing a short postmortem note in the ticket with root cause: mixed toolchains + aggressive compile flags + cached artifacts. We'll follow up on long-term: stricter toolchain pinning, CI immutability, and perf regression tests.
Andrew: Sounds good. :thumbsup:
